frontMatter.title: The Scoreboard: All 65 Languages Ranked
frontMatter.description: Every score in the 65-language coupling comparison in one place — the ranked table, the six Core and eight Ecosystem dimension sub-scores, and the complete per-language mechanism data behind each number.

frontMatterLines: description: Every score in the 65-language coupling comparison in one place — the ranked table, the six Core and eight Ecosystem dimension sub-scores, and the complete per-language mechanism data behind each number.

blocks.q: **Companion to:** [The Great Language Smackdown](index.qmd) · [The 60 Coupling Criteria](scoring-criteria.qmd) · [The Scoring Model](objective-coupling-scoring-model.qmd)

blocks.p: This page holds every number in the comparison. The first table ranks all 65 languages by Core and Ecosystem score with the star band that follows from it. The next two give the per-dimension sub-scores that produce those totals. The last table gives the mechanism-presence data behind every score, so any number can be reproduced from first principles. The criteria are on [The 60 Coupling Criteria](scoring-criteria.qmd); the arithmetic and the presence rules are on [The Scoring Model](objective-coupling-scoring-model.qmd).

*Scores from the objective model (capped-sum-per-dimension). Analysis date: June 2026; versions are the latest stable as of that date. The star rating reflects the **Core Coupling** score (the language's own coupling): 90+ = ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐, 75–89 = ⭐⭐⭐⭐, 60–74 = ⭐⭐⭐, 45–59 = ⭐⭐, below 45 = ⭐. Ecosystem coupling is shown alongside.*
*Scores from the objective model (capped-sum-per-dimension). Analysis date: June 2026. The 'Platform' column is the language's platform/domain coupling.*
This table shows how each language handles ecosystem-level coupling concerns:
*Scores from the objective model (capped-sum-per-dimension). Analysis date: June 2026.*

ul: Low score = Unpredictable GC, runtime surprises couple logic to performance
High score = Standardized tooling, rich ecosystem decouples from platform
Low score = Fragmented build systems, limited libraries couple to toolchain
High score = Backward compatible, stable, no breaking changes
Low score = Frequent breaking changes couple codebase to specific versions
High score = Works well across multiple domains
Low score = Couples to specific domains, struggles outside comfort zone
High score = Gentle, quick to productivity
Low score = Steep, productivity couples to deep expertise
High score = Concise, readable, minimal boilerplate
Low score = Verbose, boilerplate couples intent to ceremony
High score = Excellent tools, easy to test/debug
Low score = Poor tools couple understanding to manual inspection
High score = Memory safe, type safe, prevents vulnerabilities
Low score = Unsafe, couples correctness to security awareness
